chunks: 34. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Fadl ibn 'Amir, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Isma'il ibn Abu Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I am the guarantor of a house in the highest part of Paradise, a house in the middle of Paradise, and a house in the gardens of Paradise for whoever refrains from vain argument, even if he is correct.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet promise to those who avoid vain arguments?
ai.summary: In al-Tawhid, Shaykh al-Saduq cites this hadith to illustrate that even when one is factually correct, engaging in contentious debate (mura') can detract from spiritual purity, a key theme in Shia ethics regarding the purification of the self. The promise of three distinct dwellings—highest, middle, and gardens of Paradise—signifies varying degrees of reward based on the sincerity of avoiding argumentation for the sake of ego rather than truth. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on adab (etiquette) in discourse, prioritizing harmony and humility over winning verbal disputes.
